traps.trap: Only etomidate caused the adrenal crisis
traps.truth: Etomidate, ketoconazole and phenytoin all contribute: 'all of the above'.

traps.trap: Hypertensive pulmonary oedema: furosemide alone, or intubate now
traps.truth: Fluid is redistributed, not gained: high-dose nitrates + NIV first, furosemide second.

traps.trap: BP 80/50 after fluids, which drug improves output: dopamine
traps.truth: Outdated DocT key (38% chose it). Norepinephrine for pressure, dobutamine for output; dopamine only if it is the sole vasoactive option.
traps.asked: DocT QBank, 38% chose the keyed dopamine

traps.trap: Hypotension on dobutamine: switch to milrinone
traps.truth: Milrinone vasodilates more; add norepinephrine.

traps.trap: Diuretics and nitrates for RV infarction with hypotension
traps.truth: The RV is preload-dependent: fluid, then norepinephrine or vasopressin (SVR up, PVR neutral).

traps.trap: Acute AR with pulmonary oedema, BP 120/70: norepinephrine, adrenaline or furosemide
traps.truth: Nitroprusside as a bridge to surgery. IABP and β-blockers are contraindicated.

traps.trap: Inferior STEMI, new systolic murmur, oedema, BP 90/50: norepinephrine or milrinone
traps.truth: Papillary muscle rupture: IABP lowers the regurgitant fraction and bridges to surgery.

traps.trap: Low-flow, low-gradient AS: the low gradient means mild disease; treat with valvuloplasty, diuresis or fluids
traps.truth: The gradient is low because the stroke volume is low. Urgent valve replacement (TAVI); valvuloplasty is only a bridge.

traps.trap: AS patient collapses in new AF: coronary thrombosis
traps.truth: Loss of the atrial kick in a stiff, hypertrophied ventricle (taught in Shock I).

traps.trap: Takotsubo with hypotension: dobutamine or norepinephrine
traps.truth: With LVOT obstruction give phenylephrine, fluid and rate control; inotropes and vasodilators worsen the gradient.

traps.trap: EF 12% biventricular, VT, raised troponin: insert an LVAD or IABP first
traps.truth: Likely ischaemic: urgent coronary angiography with intent to revascularise.

traps.trap: High-dose dopamine, adrenaline or IABP improves survival in STEMI shock
traps.truth: Early reperfusion is the proven life-saver here; IABP and high-dose catecholamines do not improve survival (only Impella CP in selected STEMI shock, DanGer Shock, has shown a device benefit).

traps.trap: SHOCK was negative, so early revascularisation is unproven
traps.truth: 30-day mortality was similar (46.7 vs 56.0%, P 0.11), but 6-month mortality (50.3 vs 63.1%) and 1-year survival were significantly better with early revascularisation.

traps.trap: Complete revascularisation at the index PCI is preferred in shock
traps.truth: Culprit-only (CULPRIT-SHOCK, 9.5% ARR). Complete revascularisation is for non-shock STEMI (PRAMI, CvLPRIT, DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI).

traps.trap: Prior MI is part of the IABP-SHOCK II risk score
traps.truth: Prior stroke is. The six: age >73, prior stroke, glucose >191, creatinine >1.5, TIMI <3 after PCI, lactate >5.

traps.trap: VA ECMO unloads the left ventricle because it gives the most flow
traps.truth: Retrograde aortic flow raises afterload: the PV loop moves right and up; the LV may distend and need a vent.

traps.trap: IABP: usual sheath 13–14 Fr; safe beyond 2 weeks; needs an unstable rhythm
traps.truth: 7–8 Fr sheath, femoral artery ≥4 mm, days of support, regular rhythm. 13–14 Fr is Impella/ECMO.

traps.trap: Severe LV dysfunction or CAD contraindicates the IABP
traps.truth: Those are indications. Contraindications: moderate–severe AR, aortic dissection, severe aorto-iliac disease.

traps.trap: Early IABP inflation is harmless (only augmentation is lost)
traps.truth: Inflation before aortic valve closure raises afterload and LV work; late deflation is the most harmful error.

traps.trap: Device for refractory shock in rapid AF: IABP (or 'only Impella works')
traps.truth: Only the IABP needs synchrony. Key is Impella CP; strictly TandemHeart and VA ECMO are also rhythm-independent.

traps.trap: The Impella's 9 Fr catheter means a 9 Fr sheath
traps.truth: The CP pump head is 14 Fr, so the sheath is 14 Fr.

traps.trap: Pseudoaneurysm or septicaemia is the unique Impella complication
traps.truth: Both follow any femoral device; haemolysis is tied to the rotor.

traps.trap: Post-cardiotomy failure or acute myocarditis contraindicates Impella
traps.truth: Those are indications; a mechanical aortic valve and severe aortic stenosis are the bars.

traps.trap: TandemHeart is fine with a VSD, or helps isolated RV failure
traps.truth: VSD: the shunt reverses right-to-left (hypoxaemia). RV failure: the LA cannot fill. LV failure is the indication.

traps.trap: Arrest on VV ECMO: urgent conversion to VA, or withhold compressions
traps.truth: VV gives no circulatory support: standard ACLS with compressions at once; shock only VF/pVT; treat the cause.

traps.trap: Harlequin syndrome: raise sweep FiO₂, raise pump flow, or convert to VV
traps.truth: Circuit blood is already saturated and the patient still needs flow: add a jugular venous return cannula (VAV).

traps.trap: Cold pulseless leg on femoral VA ECMO: more heparin, elevation or thrombectomy
traps.truth: Immediate antegrade distal perfusion cannula into the superficial femoral artery.

mimics.tell: Milrinone raises cAMP (PDE-3 block) and so calcium; levosimendan sensitises troponin C with no rise in calcium.
Isoprenaline is pure β1 + β2: a big rate rise and a diastolic fall, so ischaemia limits it; in shock it is mainly a bridge to pacing.
Gs → cAMP → PKA; Gq → phospholipase C → IP3 + DAG.
Ryanodine receptor (and L-type channel) for contraction; phospholamban for relaxation.

mimics.pair: Levosimendan in sepsis vs on a β-blocker
mimics.tell: Suggested against in septic shock; the keyed inotrope when a chronic β-blocker blunts β-agonists.
Phenylephrine is pure α1 with no β1 chronotropy: the choice when norepinephrine drives a tachyarrhythmia.
Angiotensin II is the vasopressor drug (ATHOS-3); angiotensin I is the inactive precursor.
Both raise stroke volume; only the vasodilator does it without raising oxygen demand.
Below 90: perfusion first, diuretic later. At or above 90: vasodilator and diuretic.

mimics.pair: Wet-warm vascular type vs cardiac type
mimics.tell: Hypertension dominant (fluid redistributed): vasodilator leads. Congestion dominant (fluid gained): diuretic leads.
Sudden and hypertensive → nitrates first; days of weight gain with normal BP → diuretic first.

mimics.pair: Positive pressure in cardiogenic vs hypovolaemic shock
mimics.tell: Lower preload and afterload help the failing LV; in hypovolaemia the lost venous return drops output.
RV dysfunction or high PVR (or a β-blocker) sends you to milrinone or levosimendan, with norepinephrine.
RV: clear lungs and a high venous pressure, needs fluid and a low PVR. LV: congested lungs, needs offloading.
Both need afterload reduction; the IABP helps MR and is contraindicated in AR.

mimics.pair: Heart rate in AR vs MS
mimics.tell: Keep it fast in AR (shorter diastole, less regurgitation); slow it in MS (longer filling).

mimics.pair: LVOT obstruction vs LV pump failure
mimics.tell: LVOTO has a small hyperdynamic LV with a gradient and worsens on dobutamine.

mimics.pair: SHOCK vs CULPRIT-SHOCK vs IABP-SHOCK II
mimics.tell: Whether to revascularise early; how much to revascularise (culprit only); whether the balloon helps (no).

mimics.pair: Shock vs stable STEMI with multivessel disease
mimics.tell: Shock: culprit only. Stable: complete revascularisation.

mimics.pair: IABP vs pLVAD vs VA ECMO on the PV loop
mimics.tell: IABP: slightly lower and wider. pLVAD: smaller, shifted left. ECMO: narrower, shifted right and up.
IABP 7–8 Fr sheath; Impella CP 14 Fr.
Haemolysis is the Impella rotor; bleeding, pseudoaneurysm and limb ischaemia follow any large femoral sheath.
Impella drains the LV across the aortic valve; TandemHeart drains the LA through the septum.
TandemHeart takes already-oxygenated LA blood (no oxygenator); ECMO takes venous blood and oxygenates it.
VA returns to an artery and supports the circulation; VV returns to a vein and supports gas exchange only.

mimics.pair: Harlequin vs global hypoxaemia on ECMO
mimics.tell: Harlequin: right hand low, foot high. Both low: an oxygenator or circuit problem.

mimics.pair: LV distension vs LV recovery on VA ECMO
mimics.tell: Distension: flat arterial trace, closed aortic valve, rising PA pressures. Recovery: returning pulse pressure.

mimics.pair: IABP vs continuous-flow devices in AF
mimics.tell: Only the IABP needs a regular native rhythm and native output.

new_cards.q:
**Give the second-messenger pathway and its end effect for:**
a β1 stimulation (dobutamine): the common pathway
b The targets that give inotropy
c The targets that give lusitropy
d α1 stimulation (norepinephrine)
e The main harm of isoproterenol, and why
a: **β1 → Gs → adenylate cyclase → cAMP → protein kinase A (PKA)**
Inotropy: PKA phosphorylates the **L-type Ca²⁺ channel** and the **ryanodine receptor** → more systolic Ca²⁺ release
Lusitropy: PKA phosphorylates **phospholamban** → SERCA2a freed → faster Ca²⁺ reuptake; also **troponin I** → faster Ca²⁺ release from troponin C
**α1 → Gq → phospholipase C → IP3** (Ca²⁺ release) **+ DAG** (protein kinase C) → vasoconstriction
Isoproterenol (pure β1 + β2): rate and O₂ demand up, diastolic pressure down → **myocardial ischaemia**; in shock, mainly a bridge to pacing in bradycardia
Traps: 'myosin ATPase' or 'myosin kinase inhibition' for the heart (the keys are phospholamban and the ryanodine receptor); 'cAMP' for α1 (that is the β arm)
new_cards.why: GT7 Q83 (missed: chose myosin ATPase, key phospholamban), GT7 Q84 (missed: chose myosin kinase inhibition, key ryanodine receptor), GT7 Q85 (α1 messenger = phospholipase C), GT7 Q89 (isoproterenol harm = myocardial ischaemia). CS-29 names the receptors but not the messengers.

new_cards.topic: The patient on a chronic β-blocker
new_cards.q:
**A patient on a chronic β-blocker has low output and needs an inotrope. Give:**
a Why dobutamine and epinephrine disappoint
b The extra harm of epinephrine
c The two drugs that work past the receptor, and how
d Which one the exam keys
a: The β1 receptor is occupied: **β-agonists (dobutamine, epinephrine) are blunted** and need much higher doses
Epinephrine's β effects are blocked but its **α1 effect is unopposed** → vasoconstriction and afterload without inotropy
**Levosimendan:** sensitises troponin C to Ca²⁺ (no cAMP needed) and opens vascular K-ATP channels
**Milrinone:** PDE-3 inhibition raises cAMP below the receptor
Exam key when both are offered: **levosimendan**; if only milrinone is offered, milrinone (ESC HF guideline 2016, IIb C: levosimendan or a PDE-3 inhibitor may be considered to reverse β-blockade)
Both vasodilate: have **norepinephrine** ready for the pressure
new_cards.why: GT7 Q87 and GT8 Q82 (missed twice: chose epinephrine, key levosimendan). No card states the β-blocker rule; CS-29 gives only the mechanisms.

card_flags.issue: Card is the ESC 2016 bedside-profile algorithm (wet and cold with SBP <90: inotrope first, vasopressor if refractory). AHA 2017/SCAI and ACC/AHA 2025 practice starts norepinephrine first in hypotensive cardiogenic shock (as CS-31 on this deck says), and ESC 2021 reorganised acute HF into four presentations. Lesson teaches the card, reconciles it with CS-31 and gives a stem rule.

Two unlabelled or rounded figures. '50.3% vs 63.1%' is the 6-month mortality (30-day was 46.7% vs 56.0%, p 0.11) but the card does not say so. 'Successful vs unsuccessful PCI 35% vs 80%' is rounded: the original SHOCK report (Hochman 1999) gives 38% vs 79%; the later PCI analysis (Webb 2003) gives 39% vs 85% at one year. 'Catheter diameter 9 Fr, peak flow up to 4.3 L/min' are Impella CP figures and the card does not name the model. The pump head is 14 Fr, so the sheath is 14 Fr; a reader can take 9 Fr as the sheath size, which contradicts the IABP (7–8 Fr) vs Impella (13–14 Fr) question on CS-42.

'IABP needs a native rhythm' is the basis of GT7 Q95 (device in AF, key Impella CP). The key is narrower than the truth: TandemHeart and VA ECMO are also rhythm-independent. Card could say 'only the IABP needs a regular rhythm; Impella, TandemHeart and VA ECMO do not'.

RV shock row still lists dopamine among the pressors (AHA 2017 table) although the classic row on the same card explains why dopamine is no longer an equal choice (SOAP II). Minor inconsistency; lesson names norepinephrine or vasopressin.
